key_findings: **52 unique parent classes spanning the Sqwt UI surface get typed-delegate vftables**. Top contributors: SliderTemplate (12 across <float>+<int> + multiple event types), NumberInputBox (10), DebugControl (9), XamlElement / Esrb / ShandaLogoMenu / PhaseBase (8 each). Long tail of 27 classes with 2-6 delegates each. Confirms Sqwt's WPF-style 'event-handler per (owner, event-type) pair' pattern generalizes across the entire UI framework.

**Delegate type distribution (estimated)**: ~75% are generic EventHandler<Owner, EventArgs> bases; ~25% are derived event-specific delegates (KeyEventHandler / MouseEventHandler / MouseButtonEventHandler / PadEventHandler / RoutedEventHandler / SelectionChangedEventHandler / ClickEventHandler / DragDeltaEventHandler / AsyncCompletedEventHandler / ExecutedRoutedEventHandler / CanExecuteRoutedEventHandler / ScrollEventHandler). Each derived form has its corresponding generic base. The pattern confirmed by the lifecycle decomp (derived ctor calls parent ctor then overwrites vftable) almost certainly generalizes across the entire 167 entry set.

**Templated owner classes** (SliderTemplate<float> and SliderTemplate<int>) require special handling. SliderTemplate is the only nested-template owner observed in the EventHandler sweep. Each specialization has its own complete delegate set (12 vftables each for <float> and <int>). Suggests the Sqwt UI also supports value-typed slider controls separately rather than via type erasure.

**DragDeltaEventHandler is the 13th delegate type** beyond the 12 originally listed in the plan. Specific to slider drag interactions. Only 2 instantiations observed (SliderTemplate<float/int>) - the entire slider drag-gesture mechanism is the sole use site.

**Lifecycle functions NOT cataloged for this 167-entry set** - only vftables. The evidence (5 lifecycle functions per LuaDebugLog delegate, 12 per LuaDebugSelect) implies the same lifecycle pattern repeats across all 167 vftables here. Later work could catalog these (~500-800 additional lifecycle entries projected). Deferred as low-EV unless a specific opcode/dispatch question requires the lifecycle attribution.
